Posterior probabilities of the BDRIBS model on a grid of data

Source: R/bdribs_grid.R
bdribs_grid.Rd

Computes the posterior probability that the rate ratio exceeds rr0 under the BDRIBS model for every combination of numbers of events, exposures and background rates. The results give the contour plots and the sensitivity plots used by Waterhouse et al. (2022) to plan and interpret blinded safety reviews.

Usage

bdribs_grid(y, exposure, lambda_hp, k = 1, pt_hp = Inf, ...)

Arguments

y

Numbers of events (non-negative integers).

exposure

Exposures (positive).

lambda_hp

Background event rates of the control group.

k

Randomization ratio of study drug to control (k:1).

pt_hp

Total patient time of the historical control data, or Inf for known background rates (the default, as in the examples of Waterhouse et al., 2022).

...

Further arguments of bdribs_post (df, p_prior, rr0, cutoff).

Value

A data frame with columns y, exposure, lambda_hp and prob, one row per combination.

References

Waterhouse, B., Hartford, A., Mukhopadhyay, S., Ferguson, R. and Hendrickson, B. A. (2022). Using the Bayesian detection of potential risk using inference on blinded safety data (BDRIBS) method to support the decision to refer an event for unblinded evaluation. Pharmaceutical Statistics, 21(2), 372–385. doi:10.1002/pst.2175

See also

bdribs_post, pooled_ratio

Examples

# Example 1 of Waterhouse et al. (2022): 6, 7 or 8 events, background rate
# 3.1 per 100 patient-years, randomization 1:1
g <- bdribs_grid(y = 6:8, exposure = seq(60, 200, by = 20),
                 lambda_hp = 0.031, p_prior = c(0.5, 0.5))
head(g)
#>   y exposure lambda_hp      prob
#> 1 6       60     0.031 0.9660897
#> 2 7       60     0.031 0.9906977
#> 3 8       60     0.031 0.9977880
#> 4 6       80     0.031 0.9037555
#> 5 7       80     0.031 0.9649264
#> 6 8       80     0.031 0.9889495
